commands.name: ALLOC
commands.longDescription: The ALLOC command allows allocating datasets, files, or devices for use within the TSO session. It is used to create new datasets, allocate existing datasets, and define attributes such as space, organization, storage unit, and access parameters.
commands.examples: ALLOC DSN(MI.DATASET.TEST) NEW SPACE(5,5) TRACKS RECFM(FB) LRECL(80) BLKSIZE(8000)

commands.name: FREE
commands.longDescription: The FREE command removes the previous allocation of a dataset or resource made with ALLOC. It is useful for freeing resources that are no longer needed during the TSO session.

commands.name: LISTALC
commands.longDescription: Displays all datasets and resources currently allocated in the TSO session, including information about their status, allocation type, and attributes.

commands.name: LISTCAT
commands.longDescription: LISTCAT queries the system catalog and displays detailed information about datasets, including location, attributes, associated volumes, and usage statistics.

commands.name: DELETE
commands.longDescription: DELETE removes a dataset from the system. It can delete sequential datasets, partitioned datasets, or specific members within a PDS.

commands.name: RENAME
commands.longDescription: RENAME changes the name of an existing dataset in the catalog. It is useful for reorganizing datasets or applying naming conventions.

commands.name: COPY
commands.longDescription: COPY allows copying entire datasets or individual members within a PDS. It is common for duplicating configurations, scripts, or data.

commands.name: EDIT
commands.longDescription: EDIT opens a dataset in the TSO line editor, allowing its content to be modified directly without the need for ISPF.

commands.name: BROWSE
commands.shortDescription: Views a dataset without modifying it
commands.longDescription: BROWSE displays the content of a dataset in read-only mode. It is useful for reviewing data without the risk of altering it.

commands.name: PROFILE
commands.longDescription: PROFILE displays and allows modifying TSO session parameters for the user, such as prefixes, edit options, notifications, and job configurations.

commands.name: SEND
commands.longDescription: SEND allows sending interactive messages to other users logged onto the system. It is useful for quick communication between operators or developers.

commands.name: RECEIVE
commands.shortDescription: Receives data sent by another user
commands.longDescription: RECEIVE allows accepting datasets or data sent by another user via TSO. It is used for simple transfers between users.

commands.name: SUBMIT
commands.longDescription: SUBMIT sends a dataset containing JCL to the JES system for execution. It is one of the most commonly used commands to submit batch jobs.

commands.name: STATUS
commands.shortDescription: Displays the status of a job
commands.longDescription: STATUS queries the status of jobs submitted by the user, showing whether they are queued, executing, finished, or in error.

commands.name: TSO LOGON
commands.longDescription: TSO LOGON starts an interactive session in the TSO/E environment, allowing the user to access system resources, execute commands, and work with datasets.

commands.name: TSO LOGOFF
commands.longDescription: TSO LOGOFF closes the user's TSO session, freeing resources and terminating associated processes.

commands.name: ISPF
commands.longDescription: ISPF opens the interactive environment of system panels, menus, and utilities. It is the primary interface for editing, navigation, and advanced tools.

commands.name: HELP
commands.longDescription: HELP displays detailed information about TSO commands, syntax, parameters, and available system utilities.

commands.name: EXEC
commands.longDescription: EXEC executes scripts written in REXX or CLIST directly from TSO. It is fundamental for automating tasks and creating custom utilities.

commands.name: TIME
commands.longDescription: TIME displays the current system time and date, along with optional information about the CPU time used in the session.

Option 3.4 of the ISPF menu allows searching, listing, and managing system datasets. From this screen, you can view attributes, open datasets in EDIT or BROWSE mode, rename, delete, copy members, and perform administrative actions on them.
commands.examples: In ISPF: Option 3 → Option 4 → Enter pattern: MI.USERID.

commands.longDescription: Option 3.3 allows copying entire datasets or individual members between PDSs. It is useful for duplicating configurations, scripts, or data without the need for TSO commands.
commands.examples: In ISPF: Option 3 → Option 3 → FROM: MI.PDS1 → TO: MI.PDS2

commands.longDescription: Option 3.2 allows creating new datasets by specifying attributes such as organization, size, unit, and format. It also allows safely deleting existing datasets.
commands.examples: In ISPF: Option 3 → Option 2 → Create dataset: MI.DATASET.NEW

commands.longDescription: Option 2 opens the ISPF editor, one of the most widely used editors on the mainframe. It allows editing sequential datasets and PDS members, applying line commands, macros, and advanced editing tools.
Option 1 allows viewing datasets in BROWSE mode without modifying their content. It is ideal for reviewing JCL, logs, configurations, or data without the risk of alteration.

commands.name: TSO ISRDDN
commands.longDescription: ISRDDN displays all DDNAMEs allocated in the current session, including associated datasets, volumes, and attributes. It is useful for debugging and allocation analysis.

commands.name: TSO ISPF
commands.longDescription: The ISPF command starts the interactive ISPF environment from the TSO command line, allowing access to menus, panels, and utilities.

commands.name: TSO ISPSTART
commands.longDescription: ISPSTART allows starting ISPF directly in a specific panel, application, or utility. It is useful for automating quick access.

commands.name: TSO DSLIST
commands.longDescription: DSLIST displays a list of datasets based on a pattern. It is equivalent to option 3.4 but from the command line.

commands.name: TSO EDIT
commands.shortDescription: Edits a dataset from the command line
commands.longDescription: EDIT opens a dataset directly in the ISPF editor without navigating through menus. It allows quick editing of members or sequential datasets.

commands.name: TSO BROWSE
commands.shortDescription: Views a dataset from the command line
commands.longDescription: BROWSE allows viewing datasets in read-only mode from the TSO command line.

commands.name: TSO VIEW
commands.longDescription: VIEW displays datasets with special formatting, useful for JCL, reports, and structured data. It allows advanced viewing commands.

commands.name: TSO LISTBC
commands.longDescription: LISTBC displays the broadcast messages sent by the system, normally used for important notices, maintenance, or alerts.

commands.name: TSO LISTA
commands.longDescription: LISTA displays user attributes, including prefixes, session configurations, and job parameters.

commands.name: TSO LISTC
commands.longDescription: LISTC queries the system catalog and displays information about datasets, volumes, and attributes.

commands.name: TSO LISTDS
commands.longDescription: LISTDS displays detailed information about a dataset, including attributes, organization, size, and associated volumes.

commands.name: TSO LISTGRP
commands.longDescription: LISTGRP displays the RACF groups associated with the user, including roles, permissions, and memberships.

commands.name: TSO LISTUSER
commands.longDescription: LISTUSER displays detailed information about the RACF user, including attributes, permissions, groups, and security configurations.

commands.name: TSO LU
commands.longDescription: LU is an abbreviated alias for the LISTUSER command, used to quickly query user information.

commands.name: TSO OGET
commands.longDescription: OGET allows downloading files from the UNIX System Services (OMVS) environment to traditional datasets. It is useful for moving files between z/OS UNIX and MVS.

commands.name: DA
commands.longDescription: The DA panel displays all active datasets associated with the session, including dynamic allocations, DDNAMEs, and datasets used by executing jobs. It is useful for diagnosing allocation issues or dependencies.

commands.name: ST
commands.longDescription: The ST panel displays the active jobs in the JES2/JES3 system, including executing, queued, held, or resource-waiting jobs. It allows viewing status, owner, class, priority, and control commands.

commands.name: H
commands.longDescription: The H panel displays the history of recently completed jobs, including return code, execution time, class, and owner. It is useful for reviewing previous executions.

commands.name: I
commands.longDescription: The I panel displays general JES system information, including queue status, number of active jobs, available resources, and performance statistics.

commands.name: LOG
commands.longDescription: The LOG panel displays the JES system log, including operator messages, system events, warnings, and errors. It is fundamental for diagnostics.

commands.name: OWNER
commands.longDescription: OWNER allows filtering the job view by owner, displaying only the jobs belonging to the specified user.

commands.name: PREFIX
commands.longDescription: PREFIX filters the jobs whose name begins with a specific prefix. It is useful for locating jobs for a project or application.

commands.name: FIND
commands.shortDescription: Searches for text in the spool
commands.longDescription: FIND allows searching for text within the spool of the selected job. It is useful for locating errors, specific messages, or results.

commands.name: SORT
commands.longDescription: SORT orders the list of jobs or datasets according to a specific column, such as JOBNAME, OWNER, CLASS, or RC. It facilitates the organization of the view.

commands.name: PRINT
commands.longDescription: PRINT sends the spool content of the selected job to a printer or output dataset. It is useful for archiving or external analysis.

commands.name: PURGE
commands.shortDescription: Purges a job from the spool
commands.longDescription: PURGE completely removes a job from the spool, including its output, logs, and associated data. Only available to authorized users.

commands.name: CANCEL
commands.longDescription: CANCEL stops the execution of an active job in the system. It is useful when a job is hung, consumes too many resources, or needs to be stopped for maintenance.

commands.name: RELEASE
commands.longDescription: RELEASE frees a job that is held (HELD), allowing it to continue its normal processing in JES.

commands.name: HELD
commands.longDescription: HELD displays all jobs that are held in the system, whether by the user, by policies, or by execution conditions.

commands.name: OUTPUT
commands.longDescription: OUTPUT displays the complete spool of the selected job, including SYSOUT, compilation messages, execution, and logs.

commands.name: XDC
commands.longDescription: XDC copies the job's spool content to an MVS dataset. It is useful for analysis, archiving, or sending to other users.

commands.name: TRACE
commands.longDescription: TRACE activates or displays JES system traces, useful for advanced diagnostics, performance analysis, and debugging.

commands.name: WHO
commands.longDescription: WHO displays all users currently connected to the system, along with session, terminal, and activity information.

commands.name: DA-D
commands.longDescription: DA-D displays detailed information for each active dataset, including attributes, volumes, DDNAMEs, and allocation status.

commands.name: ST-D
commands.longDescription: ST-D displays complete details of the selected active job, including executed steps, used resources, messages, and statistics.

commands.name: ADDUSER
commands.longDescription: ADDUSER allows creating a new user profile in RACF, defining basic attributes such as name, default group, initial password, and access permissions. It is one of the fundamental commands for security administration.

commands.name: DELUSER
commands.longDescription: DELUSER removes a user profile from the RACF system, including their associations with groups and permissions. It can only be executed by administrators with sufficient authority.

commands.name: ALTUSER
commands.longDescription: ALTUSER allows modifying attributes of a RACF user, such as password, groups, special permissions, expiration, and security configurations.

commands.name: LISTUSER
commands.longDescription: LISTUSER displays detailed information of a user's RACF profile, including groups, permissions, security attributes, associated resources, and special configurations.

commands.name: LU
commands.longDescription: LU is an abbreviated alias for the LISTUSER command, used to quickly query user information.

commands.name: ADDGROUP
commands.longDescription: ADDGROUP allows creating a new RACF group, defining its owner, associated users, and security attributes.

commands.name: DELGROUP
commands.longDescription: DELGROUP removes a RACF group from the system, provided it has no associated users or active dependencies.

commands.name: ALTGROUP
commands.longDescription: ALTGROUP allows modifying attributes of a RACF group, such as owner, associated users, permissions, and security configurations.

commands.name: LISTGRP
commands.longDescription: LISTGRP displays detailed information about a RACF group, including associated users, permissions, attributes, and dependencies.

commands.name: CONNECT
commands.longDescription: CONNECT allows associating a user to a RACF group, granting them permissions and attributes defined by that group.

commands.name: REMOVE
commands.longDescription: REMOVE deletes the association between a user and a RACF group, withdrawing the permissions inherited from the group.

commands.name: RDEFINE
commands.longDescription: RDEFINE allows creating a new resource protected by RACF, specifying class, permissions, owner, and security attributes.

commands.name: RALTER
commands.longDescription: RALTER allows modifying attributes of an existing RACF resource, such as permissions, owner, auditing, or accesses.

commands.name: RDELETE
commands.longDescription: RDELETE removes a resource protected by RACF, withdrawing it from the security catalog.

deleted.name: PERMIT
deleted.longDescription: PERMIT grants access permissions for a RACF resource to specific users or groups. It is one of the most widely used commands in security administration.

deleted.name: REVOKE
deleted.longDescription: REVOKE removes permissions previously granted to a user or group on a RACF resource.

deleted.name: SEARCH
deleted.longDescription: SEARCH allows searching for resources defined in RACF based on patterns, classes, or attributes. It is useful for security audits and reviews.

deleted.name: SETROPTS

deleted.name: RVARY
deleted.longDescription: RVARY dynamically activates or deactivates RACF resource classes without restarting the system.

deleted.name: PWDCHANGE

deleted.name: ATTRIB

deleted.name: CONSOLE

deleted.name: TRANSMIT

deleted.name: TEST

Option 0 opens Settings and configures general parameters, function keys, colors, log, and list options.
Option 3.1 allows working with libraries and members, including copy, move, delete, and selection operations.
Option 3.5 provides printing and list generation functions for datasets or listings.
Option 3.6 displays information and attributes of datasets using ISPF utilities.
Option 3.7 searches for text strings within datasets and libraries.
Option 3.8 manages output lists and results generated by ISPF and TSO.
Option 3.9 allows working with ISPF command tables.
Option 3.11 provides dataset formatting functions.
Option 3.17 provides dataset listing and management utilities according to ISPF configuration.
Option 4 allows executing specific language processors in the foreground.
Option 5 generates and submits JCL to execute batch processes.
Option 6 allows executing TSO commands, CLISTs, or REXX scripts from ISPF.
Option 7 allows testing ISPF dialog components such as panels, messages, and functions.
Option 10 provides access to Software Configuration and Library Manager when installed.
Option 11 provides the ISPF Workplace environment to access functions through actions on objects.
Option 12 provides access to tools oriented toward z/OS system administration and programming.
Option 13 provides access to z/OS user applications and utilities.
